fatal_errors: The proposed method retains thermodynamic integration rather than replacing the costly DFT–reference integration with MTP-to-DFT free-energy perturbation.
The specified equimolar quinary system and approximately 0.9Tm condition do not reconstruct the BCC TaVCrW target, its 2000–2400 K range, or 0 GPa conditions.
The claimed 50% path-error reduction is unsupported and does not match the decisive target benchmark of FEP–TI agreement within 0.5 meV/atom.
The cited evidence contains no elemental or binary free-energy calculation demonstrating the required MTP/FEP accuracy.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies the central failure of EAM references and proposes a flexible, high-temperature-trained machine-learning potential to improve overlap with ab initio solid and liquid ensembles. It also provides a comparative and falsifiable simulation design. However, it omits the crucial MTP-to-DFT FEP intervention and instead continues to use thermodynamic integration, thereby missing the main source of the reported efficiency gain. It does not recover the TaVCrW composition, 2000–2400 K conditions, 3456-atom setup, PBE/LDA comparison, sub-meV training accuracy, electronic-excitation and SRO contributions, or the reported 80% savings and melting-temperature shifts. The supporting citations establish only broad plausibility for ML potentials in multicomponent solids and liquids; they do not validate the quantitative path-mismatch claim or supply the requested elemental/binary benchmark. Thus it is a meaningful but incomplete reconstruction.
